investigation: Two-Phonon Octupole Multiplets and Anharmonic Damping across Mass Regions
description: Systematic evaluation of two-phonon octupole states across doubly magic 208Pb (harmonic quadruplet 0+, 2+, 4+, 6+), semi-magic 146Gd (anharmonic fragmentation), and light actinide 224Ra (octupole condensation into static pear-shaped rotor).

boundary_1_harmonic_phonon_to_fragmented.mechanism: In doubly magic 208Pb, the 3.5-4.0 MeV shell gap suppresses background 2p-2h level density to rho ~ 6.5 / MeV, keeping spreading width Gamma^down < 9 keV and protecting the multiplet. In 146Gd, the Z=64 subshell gap is only ~1.5 MeV, boosting level density to rho ~ 82 / MeV. Strong mixing (v_mix ~ 24 keV) produces a massive spreading width Gamma^down = 295 keV that fragments the two-phonon octupole strength across >10 states, shifting the 0+ centroid upwards by +325 keV.
boundary_1_harmonic_phonon_to_fragmented.failure_signature: Severe overestimation of two-phonon transition strength and state coherence when transferring the 208Pb harmonic model to semi-magic nuclei.

boundary_2_phonon_vibration_to_static_pe.mechanism: In 208Pb, octupole phonons are dynamic harmonic vibrations around a spherical minimum. In 224Ra, the simultaneous presence of pi(i13/2 - f7/2) and nu(j15/2 - g9/2) intruder pairs near the Fermi surface makes d^2 V / d beta_3^2 < 0, condensing the system into a permanent pear shape (beta_3 = 0.14). The 3- state is not a phonon, but the I=3 member of an alternating-parity rotational band (0+, 1-, 2+, 3-, 4+, 5-). The two-phonon quadruplet does not exist.
boundary_2_phonon_vibration_to_static_pe.failure_signature: Attempting to assign multiphonon states to alternating-parity rotational bands.
